title: The pastor
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The pastor whose bulletin shares the rack reads a digest at the folding table. He laughs once, at the uncle. He asks the owner if the boy's in trouble. She says he's auditing. The pastor says that's a kind of trouble.

panels.composition: The laundromat. A PASTOR in a raincoat over a collar at the folding table with a digest. The LAUNDRY owner.

image.prompt: an older man in a raincoat over a clerical collar reading a small booklet at a laundromat folding table, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The pastor laughing once. The page: the uncle as a pear.

image.prompt: an older clergyman laughing once at a small comic booklet, black and white, no words
a clergyman speaking to a laundromat owner across a folding table, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The digest going back in the rack — the pastor putting his own bulletin behind it. The order changed. The owner sees. Leaves it.

image.prompt: close on a clergyman placing a church bulletin behind a small booklet in a wire rack, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'That's a kind.' The bulletin goes behind the digest, by the pastor's own hand.
